title: machinarium
text: Machinarium is a point, click and traditional puzzle game, Firstly pros; Lovely story, Good art style, original atmosphere/levels, speech bubble communication and also great soundtrack. I can not see any cons in this game but If I add something only negative aspect, the story is a bit short. If I briefly my comment; For an adventure game without dialogue but you get the whole story line just as easily via speech bubbles. Puzzles throughout the game are both thought-provoking and challenging, sometimes requiring the player to think outside the box to complete tasks without pushing for weird feats of skewed logic present in some games of the genre. Should the game prove to be too much of a bother, an in-built 'hint' system allows players to get some suggestions to how they can complete the task. Lastly graphically, the art style when coupled with soundtrack, it's just great. ''Old but still gold'' Recommended! title: machinarium
text: Machinarium is a cute and funny game about a robot who have had enough of bullying and corrupt systems. The main robot of the game finds itself in a landfill and after figuring out how to assemble itself begins its quest of getting back home and stopping the evildoers that has been supressing it for so long. The game features a lot of minigames and puzzles, most of which are classic logic question of geometrical type but also some new and clever ideas that are really challenging. The storyline is a bit wierd and since none of the characters really say anything, it's hard to realize where you should go after you've solved a part of the puzzle. The developers have made a smart solution to this by implementing a "tips and tricks"-help manual that you can only access after you have played a short bit of simple sidescroller. I've only had the opportunity to play it once, and since it only took me roughly five hours (even with getting stuck and trying many different paths time and again) I do not feel like this is a game that I want to own. Even though there is the option to solve some things in different order, it is a very linear game with few things that are out of the main quest. Overall I think that Machinarium is a really cute game, a nice challenge for anyone that are new to puzzle solvers or really like playing a lot of them and the design in it is really wonderful. 85% is my rating

title: mad max
text: The Mad Max game is a sandbox driving and brawling game that authentically recreates the look and feel of the films. Max has lost his signature V8 Pursuit Special to thieving Warboys led by the unfortunately named Scabrous Scrotus, and teams up with a crippled but gifted mechanic named Chumbucket, who has a vision from on high to create the perfect car: the Magnum Opus. Journey with the pair across the dried shores of a forgotten land, doing a handful of story missions and a whole heaping load of optional content. The driving physics are excellent. Those complaining about stubborn handling don't realize that the cars in Mad Max handle like actual cars- they have weight, friction, impact. You can customize the Magnum Opus to your liking, unlocking new internals and offensive attachments as you gather scrap, the game's currency, and reduce the threat level of the Warboys in each of the four major regions by destroying convoys, scarecrow markers, sniper nests and war camps. Where the Opus doesn't fit, Max can lay into his enemies with brutal hand-to-hand maneuvers, in a system not unlike the Batman: Arkham games but far less in-depth. While simply mashing attack will get you through the early fights, good use of blocks, counters and dodges will be needed later. I found the game oddly similar to Star Trek Online in this regard: while you spend much more time driving, the on foot segments will quickly make you wish you were back in the Opus. On the road, your combat options are far more powerful, and diverse: in addition to ramming enemies, with the option of using boost to enhance damage, you have a side-slam move identical to that seen in Sleeping Dogs, though it is far less effective here when compared to your other options: side flamethrowers, a harpoon that can rip wheels off cars or drivers out of the cars completely, explosive-tipped harpoons that annihilate cars outright, and of course, Max's trusty shotgun- capable of blowing a wheel off a car just as easily as it will one-shot any normal enemy while on foot. The sound quality is incredible. The shotgun makes just about the loudest bang I've ever heard in a game and when you FINALLY get your hands on the coveted "Big Chief" V8 engine near the endgame, you will hear its sublime roar and feel blessed. Dotted throughout the game are callbacks to the films, including the much-beloved Thunderdome. I cruised around the wastes for hours, only wishing the game had some better music. Mad Max succeeds where it needed to the most: Putting you in the driver's seat of the most deadly, awe-inspiring metal machine left on earth. Where it falls short is in a similar area to other "open-world" games- It is, in fact, TOO big a game. I clocked in over 60 hours and, if i were to be generous, perhaps 5 hours of that are actual story missions. Most of the game, as with Avalanche's flagship series Just Cause, is made up of optional content and there are only so many types of these activities, though the Death Run race events stand out. I found myself tuning out during long stretches of collectible farming, eventually resorting to binge-watching tv shows on netflix with the game volume turned down while I knocked activity icons off my map one by one. However, whenever I got back in the Opus, heard that engine, hit the boost, watched that blinding blue flame issue from my chrome pipes and slammed right into some unsuspecting warboy's pathetic scrapheap of a car, I remembered what I was playing and why. Mad Max is not a boring game by any stretch of the imagination, but it's a loooong one, and it has some slow stretches. Regardless, I enjoyed the better part of it- and the better part of it made me feel like I was in a world gone Mad.

title: mad max
text: Mad Max is an open world action game that is staggeringly well optimised. The core gameplay loop of driving around, fighting off patroling vehicles and frequent brawling remained enjoyable for me throughout the entire experience. In addition the game world is easily one of the best in the genre, taking the lifeless wastes of the Mad Max universe and making them interesting and visually unique, no world in gaming looks quite like this one. As great as the good parts are, the bad is of equal magnitude. The core gameplay is fun, but the structure that gameplay sits in is the worst in the entire genre, the dull routine of clearing camps, and other markers on the map got old by the end of the first zone and the structure never really improved from there, locking off entertaining upgrades behind this filler content would be a fine move if the filler wasn't so boring. In addition, much like other games sharing the Arkham/Assassins creed style parry counter combat system, I predicted that I'd have to gimp myself to make the combat entertaining. Even with intentionally not taking certain upgrades and fighting subotimally, the hand to hand gameplay fails to hold up as well as the vehicle combat, fistfights can be made entertaining, but all of the engagement has to come from the player, the combat system itself lacks Shadow of Mordors capacity for self tailored difficulty. Despite the serious shortcomings of the filler content, the main campaign is a ton of fun, though it is gated off by the godawful map marker clearing. If the game is on sale or the world is particularly enticing to you, I'd recommend picking it up, if not, don't waste your money, while the good in this game is really good, the bad is horrendous.

title: magic duels
text: As of August 2015 it's hard to recommend this FTP version of the Duels of the Planeswalkers franchise. Whilst the game itself runs at least as well as the best of its predescessors the introduction of the ability to spend real money on booster packs has completely changed the nature of the beast. Earning ingame credits is achieved via completing the short single player campaign, beating randomly generated challenges (eg. counter 20 spells), or beating real or AI players in ranked matches. Whilst this seems very reasonable, the combination of a weak starting collection of cards and the required investment of about 1-2 hours for each six card booster, means that even about 20 hours in I still feel pretty impotent when playing online. By the way, ranked matches online is currently the only way to earn currency in versus play. If you like playing with friends, forget earning cards this way. Similarly whilst two headed giant makes a return in this game, there is no reward beyond the satisfaction of seeing this game mode return. Hopefully Stainless Games listen to the feedback and introduce a small currency incentive for matches with friends and two headed giant games. I would have paid $10-15 this year again for this year's iteration of the game - I'm not going to spend $50 to enable a similar amount of content available in older games.
